newsitem.title: CANADA: Xillix gets Japan approval for LIFE system.
newsitem.headline: Xillix gets Japan approval for LIFE system.

text.p: Xillix Technologies Corp said on Thursday it won regulatory approval in Japan to market its LIFE-Lung Fluorescence Endoscopy System there for the early detection of lung cancer.
Xillix said it appointed Olympus Optical Co Ltd as the worldwide marketer of the device.

Xillix is commercializing proprietary medical imaging technology that helps diagnose early-stage cancer. When tissue containing abnormal cells is exposed to light from Xillix's fluorescence imaging devices, doctors are able to detect precancerous and cancerous cells.

Xillix said Japanese approval was a landmark because it meant the company could sell its product in all the major markets of North America, Europe and Asia. "All the national health authorities have agreed that our method of detecting and localizing lung cancer is effective," the company said.

The approval by Kohseisho, the Japanese regulatory authority, was based on data from clinical trials at the Tokyo Medical College and Kyoto University Hospital, showing that physicians' ability to detect cancer improved by 66 percent when the Xillix LIFE-Lung Fluorescence Endoscopy System was combined with conventional white light bronchoscopy.

Xillix said the clinical trials demonstrated that doctors using only conventional white light bronchoscopy were able to detect cancer in 57.4 percent of cases, while the detection rate increased to 95.1 percent when physicians used both the conventional method and the Xillix LIFE-Lung Fluorescence Endoscopy System.
"Olympus is anticipating the Xillix LIFE-Lung Fluorescence Endoscopy System to be the next breakthrough in lung cancer management," said H Morishima, General Manager of Olympus, Endoscope Division.

Lung cancer is the second leading cause of cancer deaths in Japan after cancer of the gastrointestinal tract, Xillix said. Xillix said more than 590,000 deaths from cancer were expected in the industrialized world this year and fewer than 15 percent of those affected would survive more than five years.

Xillix's second product to detect early-stage cancer in gastrointestinal tract is now in clinical development. Olympus is a development partner and will be worldwide distributor of this product, called Xillix LIFE-GI Fluorescence Endoscopy System.
